set.body:
`docs/limits.md:173-174`: "There is no caching of compiled plots. Compilation
is pure ... but nothing memoizes it for you."

Lower priority than the data/device split, and deliberately sequenced after
it: once a resize no longer redoes statistics, the remaining case for a cache
is narrower and better understood. File it now so the epic is complete, but do
not start it first -- a cache added before the split would mostly be caching
work that should not happen at all.

The precedent already exists one layer down. `CanvasRenderer.drawCached(program,
ctx, cache: CanvasRasterCache)` retains browser-native image sources across
draws by raster identity and reports hits and misses via `CanvasDrawProfile`
(`modules/canvas/README.md:14-19`). ScalaFIM's viewer does the same at its own
level with `ViewerCache` and a `ViewerProfile` carrying `hitRate`. The pattern
to copy is: caller-owned cache value, explicit capacity, observable hit rate,
never a hidden global.

Scope:

- An opt-in, caller-held cache keyed on plot identity plus context, passed in
  rather than discovered.
- A profile value reporting hits, misses and evictions, so a consumer can
  tell whether the cache is doing anything. Silent caches that never hit are
  worse than none.
- No change to purity or to output for a cache miss; `Disabled` must remain a
  first-class, zero-overhead choice, as `ViewerCache.Disabled` is.

Note the cautionary case downstream: `JavaFxViewerHost` in ScalaFIM hardcodes
`ViewerCache.Disabled` and therefore never benefits from the cache that
already exists beneath it. Whatever lands here needs a reachable path from the
public DSL, or it will go the same way.
set.title: Optional memoization for repeated compiles of unchanged plots
